author: US Updates
title: Upcoming Changes to Marine Corps Warrant Officer Program May Affect Local Service Members - NewsBreak
text:
56 minutes ago The United States Marine Corps will update its Warrant Officer (WO) Accession Program starting in 2026. The changes were announced in MARADMIN 554/25 from Marine Corps Headquarters in Washington, D.C. The updates affect how Marines apply and are selected for the Warrant Officer program.
Beginning January 1, 2026, enlisted Marines selected for WO will no longer be able to defer attendance at the Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC). Marines who cannot attend due to hardship must formally decline their selection. Those already approved for a deferral before this date may still use it for WOBC 1-27. No new deferrals will be allowed after this point.
For Reserve Other Than Active Reserve (OTAR) WO selectees, only one deferment for personal hardship will be allowed. If a Marine cannot attend The Basic School (TBS), they will remain eligible for appointment for one deferment period only.
The appointment date for WOBC attendees will also change. Starting with WOBC 1-26, the appointment date will be the first day of the month in which graduation occurs, if all requirements are met. This is intended to simplify administrative steps. The appointment date for WOBC 1-26 is April 1, 2026.
From May 1, 2026, Marines who have been passed over for promotion in their current paygrade will not be eligible to apply for WO appointment. The minimum requirement of eight years’ Time in Service (TIS) will also be enforced without waivers.
Commanders are directed to inform all eligible Marines about these changes. The new policies apply to the entire Marine Corps Total Force.
